title: A 23-year Navy doctor took military medic training and rebuilt it for Indian villages
sources: NewsGram - India Calling: NRI Doctors respond to rural India's distress
Fair Observer - India's rural healthcare inequality
caption:
A 23-year Navy doctor took military medic training. And rebuilt it for Indian villages.

Dr. Thakor G. Patel, a nephrologist and former US Navy Medical Corps captain, adapted the Navy's Independent Duty Corpsman training - used to prepare sailors to deliver care aboard ships with no doctor present - into a civilian program for rural Gujarat. Under his Sevak Project, local villagers train for roughly two months to become community health workers - screening, monitoring chronic disease, distributing medication and making referrals. What started as a single pilot village has since scaled to dozens of villages across Gujarat.

The Navy trained sailors to practice medicine without a doctor on board. He trained villagers to do the same, without a hospital nearby.
